title: Uber price target cut to $98 by BofA as delivery offsets mobility slowdown
detail:
Uber price target cut to $98 by BofA as delivery offsets mobility slowdown

BAC
UBER
UT8
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Uber Technologies Inc (NYSE:UBER, XETRA:UT8) received a price target cut to $98 from $101 from Bank of America, which maintained its "buy" rating as delivery strength offset slowing mobility growth.

Third-quarter gross bookings matched Wall Street expectations at $59.8 billion, while EBITDA of $3.0 billion exceeded the $2.9 billion consensus.

Looking ahead, management forecast fourth-quarter gross bookings of $63.25 billion to $65.25 billion and EBITDA of $3.13 billion to $3.23 billion.

Against that guidance, Bank of America trimmed its fourth-quarter gross bookings and EBITDA estimates for Uber by 0.2% each, to $64.4 billion and $3.19 billion, respectively.

The bank's longer-term revisions were mixed, with 2027 gross bookings estimates rising 0.2% to $277 billion and EBITDA falling 1% to $13.8 billion.

It also lowered projected adjusted earnings per share to $4.24 from $4.35, driving the target cut while retaining a valuation multiple of 23 times earnings.

Despite the mobility slowdown, management said supply incentives had stabilized growth in that business in October.

Looking further ahead, Uber expects 700 fully driverless vehicles by year-end and more than 2,000 by year-end 2027, with deployment accelerating in 2028.

To support investment, Bank of America expects $12.4 billion in free cash flow in 2027, providing capacity for autonomous vehicle spending and share repurchases.

The bank sees greater visibility into driverless vehicle supply supporting potential valuation gains, underpinning its positive stance despite the earnings reductions.

Near-term catalysts identified by Bank of America include US driverless launches, additional city announcements, infrastructure development and potential automaker agreements using Nuro/Nvidia technology.

title: Costco retains BofA "buy" as October US comps rise 8.1%

Costco retains BofA "buy" as October US comps rise 8.1%

Trading disclosure
Costco retains BofA "buy" as October US comps rise 8.1% Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Costco Wholesale Corporation (NASDAQ:COST, XETRA:CTO) US comparable sales accelerated in October, prompting Bank of America to maintain its "buy" rating.

US comparable sales excluding gasoline price changes rose 8.1%, with growth improving from September on both a year-over-year and two-year stacked basis, BofA said.

Across the broader business, Costco's total sales increased 12.6% in the four weeks ended November 1, while comparable sales excluding gasoline price changes and currency effects rose 7.3%.

That companywide comparable sales growth included a 4.1% increase in traffic, versus September's 4.7%, and 3.1% growth in average spending on the same adjusted basis, versus 2.8%.

Digital growth strengthened more sharply, with digitally enabled comparable sales excluding currency effects rising 22.6%, up from 19.1% in September.

Merchandise category performance remained consistent, with nonfood comparable sales rising by a high-single-digit percentage, led by gift cards, sporting goods and housewares.

Costco's fresh food comparable sales grew by a mid- to high-single-digit percentage, supported by meat and bakery, while food and sundries rose by a mid-single-digit percentage.

Beyond those sales trends, BofA cited the retailer's value strategy and higher-income core customers as reasons for confidence in continued market share gains amid price sensitivity.

Regional performance was less uniform, as Canadian comparable sales growth, excluding gasoline price changes and currency effects, slowed to 3.5% from 4.9%, reflecting softer economic conditions, according to BofA.

Looking ahead, BofA said DoorDash and Uber Eats gift card sales could support comparable sales following September's nationwide expansion of same-day delivery partnerships.

title: AppLovin's Q3 Beat Limits Downside, But Long-Term Growth Visibility Remains Uncertain, BofA Says
detail:
PREMIUM
AppLovin's Q3 Beat Limits Downside, But Long-Term Growth Visibility Remains Uncertain, BofA Says
MT Newswires
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 8:36 AM PST 1 min read
APP
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

AppLovin (APP) delivered a significant Q3 revenue beat, supported by the partial rollout of its new predictive model architecture, while improved infrastructure efficiency helped restore gross margins, BofA said in a Thursday note.

According to the report, revenue rose 14% sequentially to $2.19 billion, significantly beating expectations, while gross margin rebounded about 700 basis points to 89.6% as infrastructure efficiencies offset higher computing costs. Consumer revenue increased 11% sequentially to $348 million.

For Q4, revenue guidance implies sequential growth of about 10% at the high end. BofA remained cautious about the timing of further model improvements, noting that management maintained its 30% long-term growth target but could not specify when the full rollout would occur.

BofA raised its 2027 revenue growth estimate to 25% from 23% but said further evidence is needed to support sustained hypergrowth, given increased execution risks as the business scales.

BofA maintained its neutral rating on the stock while raising its price target to $380 from $325.

AppLovin shares were up 28% in Thursday trading.

title: Arista Networks gets BofA backing as 2027 growth outlook tops Street
detail:
Arista Networks gets BofA backing as 2027 growth outlook tops Street

Trading disclosure
Arista Networks gets BofA backing as 2027 growth outlook tops Street Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Arista Networks Inc (NYSE:ANET) drew higher estimates from Bank of America after its 2027 growth outlook topped Wall Street expectations, with the broker reiterating its "buy" rating and $240 price target.

Management forecast 39% revenue growth in 2027 against the Street's 28%, following third-quarter growth of 59%, above expectations of 44%.

That momentum is expected to continue into the fourth quarter, with growth guidance of 59% running nearly 15 percentage points above expectations, the broker said.

Bank of America raised its forecasts to reflect stronger demand, although peer valuation declines prompted a lower target multiple of 41 times estimated 2027 earnings, versus 49 previously.

Supporting Arista Networks' outlook, management expects AI revenue to double from $3.5 billion in 2026 to $7 billion in 2027, alongside 60% campus growth.

The broker also sees potential upside because it calculates that guidance implies only about 10% growth in enterprise switching.

Behind the AI forecast, Arista expects to participate in more than 10 gigawatts of new distributed AI capacity by the end of 2027, excluding existing data centers.

Using Dell'Oro assumptions, Bank of America estimates that capacity represents about $15 billion in underlying switching content.

Within that opportunity, Arista Networks expects connections between data centers, or "scale-across" applications, to account for more than one-third of AI revenue in 2027.

Management also expects operating margins near 49% in the fourth quarter and 2027, suggesting continued profitability despite AI investment, following a third-quarter margin of 49.1%.

Against that strong outlook, deferred revenue presents a caution, with sequential growth slowing from 15% to 10% before a 0.5% decline.

Product deferred revenue fell $86 million in the third quarter, although the broker said customer acceptance milestones may partly explain the slowdown.

Providing a counterweight, purchase commitments rose 18% sequentially, while management expects deferred revenue to remain at or above last year's $5.4 billion, supported by product launches and new applications.

Shares of Arista Networks rose about 6% on Wednesday.

title: Mid-Cap Banks to Benefit From Asset Repricing, BofA Says

BAC

Trading disclosure

Mid-cap banks are largely expected to benefit from fixed-asset repricing over the next 12 to 15 months, supporting continued earnings growth, with investors increasingly rewarding sustainable earnings improvement over quarterly beats, BofA Securities said in a Wednesday note.

In Q3, 70% of mid-cap banks beat earnings per share estimates, with 56% due to revenue, 59% on expenses, and 65% on lower credit costs, analysts said.

Popular (BPOP) and Columbia Banking System (COLB) are BofA's top picks as they have visible net interest margin support at attractive valuations.

Analysts said Texas Capital Bancshares (TCBI) was the "clearest winner" of the earnings cycle, adding that Central Bancompany (CBC) and Prosperity Bancshares (PB) shares outperformed amid increased confidence in repricing, cost savings, and forward earnings visibility.

BofA increased Central Bancompany's price objective to $36.50 from $33, Prosperity Bancshares' to $82 from $79, and Washington Trust Bancorp's (WASH) to $37 from $36. It lowered Associated Banc-Corp's (ASB) price objective to $32 from $34 and Commerce Bancshares' (CBSH) to $68 from $71.
